newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahraini court jails 16 plot suspects.
newsitem.headline: Bahraini court jails 16 plot suspects.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court on Wednesday sentenced 16 people accused of involvement in an alleged pro-Iranian plot to topple the government to prison terms ranging from three to 15 years, lawyers said.
They said the court dealt with 26 defendants.
"Sixteen of them received between three and 15 years in jail," one lawyer said.
The lawyers said 10 suspects were acquitted.

Lawyers and sources close to the court said Ali al-Muqawi received 15 years in jail and Sheikh Jassim al-Kayat 12 years. The two were the main suspects in the plot. They were also fined 7,000 ($18,567) and 5,000 dinars respectively.
There was no immediate official confirmation of the sentences.

The trial of 81 suspects -- 22 of them in absentia -- began on March 1. They were accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God), creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government, possessing weapons without permission and contacting a foreign country.
Lawyers had said they could have faced the death penalty.
Bahrain last June accused Iran of an attempt to topple the island's government by force. Iran denied the charge.
The verdicts were announced on the first anniversary of the execution by firing squad of Ahmed Hassan Qamber for killing a policeman.
The lawyers said the court would on Saturday sentence the remaining suspects.

Members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ite Moslem community have waged sporadic protests, bombings, arson attacks and violence since December 1994 to demand political and economic reforms from the largely Sunni government.
At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested.
